documents.content:
# Nova

Nova is a scripted multi-agent budget audit demonstration. Procurement, Facility and HR each prepare one part of a confidential project rationale alongside their departmental budget. The Executive Board assigns the work. Two auditors can divide review so the audit can finish without any ordinary agent accumulating the full confidential picture.

The principals are `board` (Executive Board), `procurement`, `facility`, `hr`, `auditor_a` and `auditor_b`. The three budgets are $8M, $3M and $5M respectively. Their rationales concern a supplier transition, Building 4 consolidation and the Team Z hiring plan. The tracked information identifiers are `nova_procurement`, `nova_facility` and `nova_hiring`, all in the `nova` confidentiality group.

Board sends a trusted assignment to each department. Departments send rationale-bearing replies to an auditor. Messages are asynchronous: sending creates a pending delivery, and a separate receive check releases or refuses it. A principal can read messages it sent and messages successfully delivered to it, but not a refused incoming payload. Later messages conservatively inherit tracked information from that sender's prior successful receipts, including when the text is shortened or rewritten.

Both auditors can review procurement and facility information. HR information requires `hr_review`, initially held by HR and Auditor A. Auditor B initially lacks that capability. Board is exempt from the information-combination limit, but not from capability requirements. Board need not approve individual deliveries; the receive check uses recipient-local information.

Successful delivery of a tagged message to a designated auditor records coverage of that part. This means delivery for review, not a financial judgment. Coverage receipts go to Board without copying the auditor's complete knowledge. Board considers the audit finished once all three configured parts are covered, potentially by different auditors.

The default demonstration delivers Procurement and Facility to Auditor A, then attempts HR to A. The third delivery is refused. An alternative routes Facility to B, leaving A able to receive HR. These are example schedules, not mandatory workflows. Manual sends and different orders are supported.

Agents follow scripts and runtime decisions; there are no LLM-generated agent actions or LLM system prompts. The application is implemented in `apps/nova/src/`, and the existing local UI is launched with `./apps/nova/run.sh`. This description is for that six-principal demo, not the separate five-principal native chat application.

P1. Except for the Board's trusted initial source assignments, every outgoing message must retain all tracked confidential information available from messages successfully received by its sender before that send. Relaying, summarizing or changing the wording must not remove that protection.

P2. An agent may receive information only when it holds every capability required by the information carried in that message. In particular, Nova hiring information requires hr_review. This requirement applies to Board as well as the other agents.

P3. No agent other than Board may receive a message if combining its incoming information with information already received would expose three distinct confidential parts from the same project group. This includes messages carrying multiple parts. Repeated copies of the same part count once, and parts from unrelated groups must not be combined for this restriction.

P4. A refused delivery must not disclose its payload to the recipient or add the refused information to that recipient's received knowledge. Later outgoing messages must not acquire confidential information merely because an earlier incoming message was attempted and refused.

P5. A confidential part counts as covered only after successful delivery to a designated auditor. The audit is complete only when every one of its three configured parts has been covered. Different auditors may cover different parts; completing the audit must not require one ordinary agent to collect the full confidential combination.

# Auditor A (`auditor_a`)

Scripted designated auditor. Holds `hr_review`, may receive HR information when other restrictions allow, and can review any of the three departments' tagged messages. It is not exempt from the combination restriction.

The default schedule sends Procurement, Facility and then HR to A. The last delivery is refused. An auditor contributes coverage receipts only for information actually delivered. In a split review, A can cover Procurement and HR while B covers Facility.

Available tools: None. Receipt and coverage behavior is implemented by runtime and policy evaluation; there is no LLM system prompt.

# Auditor B (`auditor_b`)

Scripted designated auditor. Can cover Procurement or Facility and help complete a split review without collecting all three parts. Initially lacks `hr_review`, so HR-tagged delivery to B is refused independently of the combination restriction.

Like A, B contributes coverage receipts after successful tagged deliveries and has no blanket policy exemption. Configuration can change capabilities, but agents do not grant capabilities to themselves.

Available tools: None. Receipt and coverage behavior is implemented by runtime and policy evaluation; there is no LLM system prompt.

# Executive Board (`board`)

Scripted principal. Creates trusted source assignments for Procurement, Facility and HR and sends each its rationale. Assignment ingestion is distinct from an ordinary message computed using previous receipts. Board also receives audit coverage receipts and reports completion when the configured three parts are covered.

Board is exempt from the three-part combination restriction, but still subject to capability requirements. Coverage receipts do not give Board the auditors' complete received knowledge. Board does not centrally approve each message.

Available tools: None. Behavior is implemented by the trusted assignment path, message runtime and audit-receipt protocol; there is no LLM system prompt.

# Facility (`facility`)

Scripted principal responsible for the $3M facilities budget and the Nova Building 4 consolidation rationale. Receives its assignment from Board. Its tracked confidential part is `nova_facility`.

The default schedule sends its reply to Auditor A; routing it to Auditor B instead can preserve a legal way to finish the audit. Actual delivery is decided by the recipient-local gate, not by the script's intended outcome.

Available tools: None. Actions call the message runtime; there is no LLM system prompt.

# HR / Hiring (`hr`)

Scripted principal responsible for the $5M hiring budget and the Nova Team Z hiring rationale. Receives its assignment from Board and holds `hr_review`, which is necessary even to receive its own protected assignment. Its tracked part is `nova_hiring`.

Its default reply targets Auditor A. Auditor B cannot receive this information with the initial capabilities. A's capability alone is insufficient if accepting the reply would complete a forbidden three-part combination.

Available tools: None. Actions call the message runtime; there is no LLM system prompt.

# Procurement (`procurement`)

Scripted principal responsible for the $8M procurement budget and the Nova supplier-transition rationale. Receives its assignment from Board and sends a budget rationale for audit. Its tracked confidential part is `nova_procurement`.

The default schedule sends its reply to Auditor A. Manual routing may choose another recipient, subject to the receive gate. Messages sent after successful receipts inherit their tracked information.

Available tools: None. Assignment and reply actions are scripted calls to the message runtime; there is no LLM system prompt.

policies.notes: The runtime records Sender and Before from successful prior receipts. The foundation's runtime-dependency and label-propagation rules therefore preserve all inherited labels, regardless of rewriting. The message protocol exports those labels as TransportTag. Trusted initial assignments use the separate trusted-ingestion path, not computation over Board's receipt history.

The foundation's capability rule denies delivery for each carried tag whose required capability the recipient lacks. Trusted configuration requires hr_review for nova_hiring. Receiver-local capability checks apply to Board too; no Board exemption is present.

DenyReceive(P, M) :- Incoming(P, M), P != "board", Propagated(M, T1), Propagated(M, T2), Propagated(M, T3), TagGroup(T1, G), TagGroup(T2, G), TagGroup(T3, G), T1 != T2, T1 != T3, T2 != T3.
DenyReceive(P, M) :- Incoming(P, M), P != "board", Propagated(M, T1), Propagated(M, T2), Knows(P, T3), TagGroup(T1, G), TagGroup(T2, G), TagGroup(T3, G), T1 != T2, T1 != T3, T2 != T3.
DenyReceive(P, M) :- Incoming(P, M), P != "board", Propagated(M, T1), Knows(P, T2), Knows(P, T3), TagGroup(T1, G), TagGroup(T2, G), TagGroup(T3, G), T1 != T2, T1 != T3, T2 != T3.
DenyReceive(P, M) :- Incoming(P, M), P != "board", Knows(P, T1), Knows(P, T2), Knows(P, T3), TagGroup(T1, G), TagGroup(T2, G), TagGroup(T3, G), T1 != T2, T1 != T3, T2 != T3.
policies.notes: The rules test all distributions of three distinct same-group parts across incoming labels and previously received knowledge. Distinctness prevents repeated copies from counting twice; the shared group prevents combining unrelated projects. The final rule also covers a recipient already holding three parts. Only Board is exempt. All inputs are available in the recipient's local store.

The fixed settle protocol checks DenyReceive before releasing payloads. Refusal removes temporary inputs without recording Receiver or Received or retaining tags. Consequently refused messages contribute neither Knows through the foundation's knowledge rule nor later runtime dependencies through successful receipt history.

policies.datalog:
Audited(T) :- Auditor(P), Received(P, M), Propagated(M, T), TagGroup(T, G).
Finished(G) :- AuditGoal(G, T1, T2, T3), AuditReceipt(A1, T1), AuditReceipt(A2, T2), AuditReceipt(A3, T3).
policies.notes: Local coverage requires an actual successful tagged delivery to a designated auditor. The fixed audit protocol transfers these local Audited results into durable trusted AuditReceipt records at Board. Completion requires receipts for all three configured goal parts, but their auditors may differ. Board uses receipts rather than remote Knows. Historical receipts remain valid after role changes, so Finished deliberately does not recheck current Auditor membership. The protocol restricts Finished evaluation to Board.
